d:
Filter chip with an optional count badge. State × Badge.

Used for the expense category filter. Only categories that have data that month are rendered, so the strip length varies. State=Selected is the active filter; Badge=True shows how many entries match.

Primary action control. Variant × Severity × Size × State.

Filled = the single main action on a screen. Outline = secondary. Ghost = tertiary and inline actions.

Severity=Danger is only for destructive actions, which must follow the two-tap confirm pattern: first tap shows "¿Eliminar?", second deletes. Never delete on one tap.

Labels use Control/SM–XL, whose line height is 100% so the text centres in the frame.

Mobile-only entry point for creating records. State = Closed | Open.

Open reveals three FABAction items and dims the page behind with surface/scrim. The plus rotates 45° into a close icon rather than swapping glyphs, so the button never changes shape.

Sits above the bottom nav, not inside it. Only visible on the Mes, Dashboard and Cuentas views. On desktop the same actions live in MonthNav's "Agregar" popover.

One item of the FAB speed-dial. Card surface with a border so it separates from the dimmed page behind it.

The icon takes interactive/primary — the only colour in the row, which is what makes the three items scannable at a glance.

The three are always Ingreso · Gasto · Movimiento, in that order, staggered 40ms apart from the FAB outward.

Icon-only action. Same four axes as Button.

Row actions are ALWAYS visible — never hidden behind hover. Use SM in filter bars and list rows, MD as the default.

Every instance needs an accessible label in code; the icon alone is not a name.
Account chip attached to an income, expense or transfer row. Colour maps to the account/1–4 token pairs (ARQ · Toptal · Bancolombia · other).

Generic label chip. Variant × Color × Icon.

Variant=Filled paints badge/{semantic}/background; Variant=Outline paints badge/{semantic}/border with no fill. Same geometry, same six token families — this used to be two component sets (Badge filled, Status outline), and the filled one had zero instances in the whole file. Filled and outline are a treatment, not two components.

Outline is the entry-state treatment: scheduled, unconfirmed, overdue. Filled is a plain label.

Colour here is decorative. The moment a badge carries meaning — an account, a category, a currency — use the specific component instead, so the semantic token layer stays the source of that meaning.

One variant per expense category — 15, mapped 1:1 to EGRESO_CATEGORIAS in code.

Colour comes from category/{id}/default and /surface. In dark mode the surface is -950 and the text -300, uniformly; connectivity and other are the documented exception because their neutral -950 disappears against the page background.

USD or COP marker. Used wherever an amount could be misread as the wrong currency — this product lives in two.

Paints currency/usd/* and currency/cop/*, which alias account/1 and account/3. A currency is not an account: they share a colour by convention, and the split means moving the account palette does not silently repaint the currency chip.
Star toggle on an account. Favourites pin as compact cards on Resumen and sort first in every account picker.
A 6px dot. Presence marker: unconfirmed entry, unread notification. Carries no colour meaning of its own.
Counter on the header bell. Primary counts overdue and due-today only. Secondary is upcoming (next 7 days) and is deliberately not counted in the badge number.
Live TRM chip in the header. Informative only — every calculation uses the month's stored TRM, never this one.

Account card. Type × State × Size.

Each type shows different data, which is why this is one set and not four components: Bank Account adds the estimated monthly yield, Credit Card shows limit, debt, % used and the cut/payment dates, Savings shows the CDT maturity countdown, Cash has neither number nor rate.

The account type is locked after creation — the card never needs to handle a type change.

DEPRECATED — superseded by the AccountCard set. 180×102, no variants, and it duplicated the name of the set, which made both unusable from the asset panel.

Remap any remaining instances to the set, then delete.

The generic surface everything else sits on. Footer = True/False.

Slots: header (title + description), content, footer. The footer carries a top border and is the only part that is optional.

This is the base of AccountCard, SavingsCard and SectionCard — if the card chrome changes, it changes here.

Where the gross income of the month went, as one bar. Not a chart component — it always shows the same four segments in the same order: Obligaciones · Provisiones · Gastos · Neto libre.

Segments come from kpi/*/default, so a segment can never drift from the KPI card it corresponds to. Hovering one dims the rest to 40% and reveals its amount on the right.

Segments with a zero amount are not rendered, so the bar can have between one and four.

A month KPI: label, figure, and a breakdown on hover.

Label uses Label/Micro, figure uses Amount/Hero. Clicking a KPI jumps to its tab — the card is a control, not just a readout.

The strip is adaptive: Tributarias and Provisiones disappear entirely for the empleado profile, so the row must read correctly with three cards or five.

A single figure with its label. Sub = True/False.

Sits on surface/wrap/subtle, not on a card — it is meant to be embedded inside another card, not to stand alone. That is what separates it from KPI-Card, which is a control you can click.

The figure uses Amount/Large; the label Detail/Large.

Savings account card. Type × State × Size.

Only savings-type accounts appear in the Ahorros view. CDT variants show a maturity countdown.

Known inconsistency: the variant values are still Spanish (Cuenta | CDT | Inversión) while every other set in the file is English.

THE most used container in the product — 10 files import it. Action = True/False.

A Card with an icon + title header and an optional action on the right. The title uses Heading/Group, which is the most common header in the app precisely because of this component.

Every list section in the Mes view is one of these.

The Gastos tab — the largest container in the system: category chips with counts, sort and filters, and a distribution bar.

The strip of category chips only renders categories that have data that month, so its length changes month to month and the layout has to survive one chip or fifteen.

The Ingresos tab of the Mes view. Device = Mobile | Desktop.

Lists the month's incomes with account badges and a gross total converted with that month's TRM.

The Provisiones tab: primas, cesantías, vacaciones, computed on gross income with provisions enabled.

Conditional in the same way as TaxContainer. Users can add their own provisions, so the list length is not fixed.

The Tributarias tab: salud, pensión, ARL and retención, plus the FSS row that appears automatically when IBC ≥ 4 SMMLV.

Conditional — the whole tab is absent for the empleado profile. Also holds the payment calendar keyed to the last digits of the cédula.
The Movimientos tab. Transfers between own accounts, with the effective-TRM calculator.

Empty state for a list that has no entries yet. Media = Icon | None.

The dashed border is deliberate: it says “this container is real but has nothing in it”, which a solid border would not. It is the one place in the system that uses a dash.

Always carries an action. An empty state without a way out is a dead end.

Something failed and has to be retried. Sibling of Empty: same anatomy, different intent.

The border is SOLID on purpose. Empty’s dashed border means “a real container, but empty” and is the only dash in the system; an error is not empty.

The media uses bg/danger-subtle with the icon in fg/danger — the tint, not the emphasis: a failed load is not a catastrophe.

The description reminds the reader that the data is still on the device. The app is local-first and a view failure puts nothing saved at risk.

A 1px rule on border/default.

Only for separating peers inside one container. Between containers the gap does the work — a rule there reads as a border that failed.

Loading placeholder. Uses bg/disabled — the same token as a disabled control, because both mean “here but not usable yet”.

Matches the shape of what is coming, never a spinner. A spinner tells you to wait; a skeleton tells you what you are waiting for.

Work in progress after a user action. Does NOT replace Skeleton: a skeleton says what content is coming, and can only do so when there is a shape to anticipate. When someone presses a button there is nothing to anticipate — the only thing to confirm is that the click was handled.

Colour: prefer INHERITING. A spinner inside a control should take currentColor for the head and currentColor at 20% for the track, so it can never disagree with the label beside it — a danger outline button has a red label and neither fixed tone is red. spinner/head/on-solid and /default exist for a spinner standing alone with no label to inherit from.

Renamed 2026-08-22: the tokens were on-dark / on-light, which named the BUTTON and not the surface — their values invert between modes, so on-dark was light in light mode. Dev found it.

Rotation: motion/duration/spin on motion/easing/spin.

Transient confirmation. Inverts against the page via bg/inverse + fg/on-inverse.

Centred at the bottom, above the mobile nav and above any open sheet — it has to stay visible over a drawer.

No action, no dismiss button. If the user needs to do something about it, it is not a toast.

The twelve account colours, two rows of six, spread across the full width of whatever holds them.

No caption and no colour name on screen. Choosing an account colour is a preference, not a task with a right answer, so nothing is lost when two hues are hard to tell apart — and the selection is carried by a check mark, not by colour, so 1.4.1 is satisfied without words. The names survive as each swatch’s accessible name.

No “in use” marker. Colours repeat across accounts by design; an unexplained dot on a choice with no wrong answer reads as a restriction.

Two explicit rows, not a wrapping grid: wrap packs as many as fit and becomes eight per row at this width. Six per row is a decision.

Carries no label of its own. Wrap it in Field.

One colour a user can pick for an account. The chip is the accent at full strength; the tint the avatar uses is a separate token and is not shown here, because it is invisible against a light canvas.

Geometry: 44px hit target, 36px disc, radius/full. 44 rather than the 40 it started at — these sit close together and the minimum is a floor, not a target. The 4px inset is the gap the selection ring needs so a ring in the same accent still reads as a ring.

Selected draws a 2px ring in the account’s own accent. Not the brand colour: the ring has to survive eleven other hues beside it. Hover is a neutral 1px border/strong ring — a hover ring in the accent is one step from reading as selected.

Every swatch needs an accessible name (Morado · Celeste · Esmeralda · Lima · Ámbar · Fucsia · Azul · Verde · Índigo · Naranja · Rosa · Turquesa). The name is not shown; a screen-reader user still has to hear one.

One account in the onboarding list. The leading check is not a choice: it says the account is included, and it is always on — what varies is whether the user can take it out.

Type=Fixed is an account the product includes and nobody can remove (Efectivo). Type=User is one the person added: it carries the brand wash, the primary border and the remove button. The difference in weight is deliberate — it marks what is theirs.

Show badge turns on the currency chip; Show description the second line. Focused is the two-ring shadow, clipped behind the node so it does not tint the translucent fill (see 19-choice-rows.md).

Month grid inside the date popover. DatePicker was retired into Field + Input on 2026-08-20, so the popover now belongs to a date-configured Input, not to a component of its own. Spanish weekday initials, Monday first — es-CO, not the Sunday-first US default.

One selected day, today outlined. Days outside the month are dimmed but still pickable.

Single day cell in the Calendar month grid.

State is a property, not a baked layer — hover, focus-visible and disabled exist here and nowhere else. “outside” days belong to the adjacent month and remain pickable, so they are active text and meet 4.5:1.

A single choice among options, drawn as a row. It is a radio in row form: the choice is exclusive and the state lives in the group, so it carries the system Radio instead of drawing its own mark.

Show media turns on the leading tile — use it when the options are kinds of thing rather than values, because an icon is what gets scanned before the words. Show description turns on the second line; a row with no description is a value, a row with one is a decision.

State and Selected are separate axes and are visible at the same time. Focused is the two-ring shadow, the same one CurrencyRadio uses; it never replaces the selection.

Choosing one currency among several, in card form. It is a radio, not a button: the choice is exclusive and the state lives in the group, not in the card. That is why it carries the system Radio inside instead of drawing its own mark.

The flag is not decoration: in an app that shows two currencies at once, it is what gets recognised before anything is read. Its colours stay raw on purpose — they belong to a country, not to us — so it lives in brand-mark/flag, exempt from C1 (see design-system/docs/16-marks.md).

Selected=True paints bg/brand-alpha-10 with a bg/brand border; State=Focused is the ring and never replaces the selection: you can be focused without having chosen, and both have to be visible at once.

A form field: the label, the control, and the message. Built 2026-08-20 because the system had four form components and four different answers about labels — Input, Select and DatePicker had none at all and were letting the placeholder do the job, at 2.56:1 contrast and gone as soon as the user types.

The control is an INSTANCE SWAP: swap in Input, Select or anything else — including an Input configured as a date or money field, which is what replaced DatePicker and MoneyInput. The field’s own visual state (focus, disabled) belongs to the control; this wrapper only knows whether the message is a hint or an error.

The control slot HUGS. It was FIXED at 40px — the height of an Input — which silently clipped anything taller the moment one was swapped in: AccountColorPicker lost its second row and the drawer looked like it had six colours. An instance-swap slot cannot carry the height of its default occupant.

Text field. HasValue × State × Size.

MD (36px) is the standard for every form. SM (28px) belongs to filter bars only. All controls in the same row must share a size — an input, a select and a date picker side by side at different heights is the most common visual bug in this product.

Overflow: the value fills the remaining width and truncates with an ellipsis; the icons hug and never shrink. A value longer than the field must not widen it.

Single choice within a group. 20px, 2px ring, filled with bg/brand and a check when selected.

Selected is also what a locked, always-on row looks like — the “Efectivo” account in onboarding is drawn with this, not with a separate indicator, because it means the same thing to the reader: this one is in.

No Disabled and no Hover: nothing in Neto disables one option of a group, and the whole row is the hit target, so the ring itself never carries a hover. Both come back as decisions if a screen needs them.

Created 2026-08-17 while mapping the onboarding flow, where this was hand-rolled five times.

One segment of a segmented control. Compose them inside SegmentedControl — a segment on its own is not a control.

Selected paints bg/brand with primary-foreground text; Default and Hover have no fill and differ only in text colour. There is deliberately NO Disabled state: the two segmented controls in the product (account type, currency) never disable a segment, and designing one would be inventing a state nobody asked for.

Built 2026-08-17 from OnboardingView.tsx, where this control was hand-rolled twice out of raw button elements with two different paddings. This unifies them at 10/6; if a tighter one is genuinely needed it comes back as a Size property, not as a second drawing.

Segmented control: a small, flat set of mutually exclusive choices, all visible at once. Use it when the options are few and comparable; use Select when they are many or long.

Items=3 is the account-type picker (Cuenta · Efectivo · Crédito), Items=2 is the currency picker (COP · USD). Segments FILL the track, so every option is the same width and the control reads as one object rather than as buttons in a row — resize the instance, do not resize the segments.

Geometry: container radius/full, bg/chrome with a border/subtle hairline, padding spacing/4, gap spacing/2. The selected segment is bg/brand-alpha-20 with a border/brand-alpha-50 border and fg/on-subtle text — a wash, not a solid fill. A solid brand fill forces white text and makes the control the loudest thing on screen, which is wrong for a picker inside a form. Both states are 34px because the border is always drawn, transparent when inactive; otherwise selecting shifts its neighbours by 1px.

Dropdown trigger. Deliberately shares the axes and heights of Input so the two align in a row.

In code the height comes from the size prop or from data-size=“none” — never from an h-* class, which loses to the data-attribute specificity and silently does nothing.

Overflow: the value fills the remaining width and truncates with an ellipsis; the icons hug and never shrink. A value longer than the field must not widen it.

Toggle for a boolean setting. State × Disabled.

Track 36×20, thumb 16. The off track is an alpha (black 20% light / white 30% dark) so it reads on any surface — a solid grey would disappear on a card and shout on the page background.

Used for “aplicar provisiones”, “gasto recurrente” and the deduction toggles. Never for an action — a switch commits immediately, it has no confirm step.

Tab in the Mes view navigation: Ingresos · Gastos · Movimientos · Tributarias · Provisiones.

The last two only exist when the user has that deduction group enabled, so the strip must read correctly with three tabs or five. Do not design for five and hope.
User avatar, SM–XL. Falls back to initials on the avatar/background token when there is no image.

Sized wrapper around a Lucide glyph. size = XS 12 · S 16 · M 20 · L 24, bound to size/icon/*.

The glyph itself is the Glyph property — an instance swap wired to the 76 icons on the Icons page. Change the glyph there, never by detaching.

Every icon in the product goes through this component, which is why size is a variant and not a manual resize: an icon at 17px is a bug, not a choice.
Account-type glyph. One variant per account type, so the icon can never disagree with the account type it sits next to.
Mobile tab bar, 412×58. The FAB with speed-dial sits above it.
A single bottom-nav tab. State = Default | Selected.

A sidebar row. State × Expanded.

40px tall, 12px radius, px-3 py-2 expanded and p-3 centred when collapsed.

Selected is cyan. Hover stays neutral on purpose: two cyan states next to each other read as two selections.

Naming nit: State values mix casing.

Month stepper at the top of the Mes view. Device = Mobile | Desktop.

The arrows are the only way to change month — there is no date picker here, because the app is built around one month at a time and jumping is rare.

Prev is disabled in January and next in December: the store holds one calendar year. Touch targets are 44px on mobile and 32px on desktop.

Desktop adds the "Agregar" popover, which carries the same three actions the FAB carries on mobile.

Desktop navigation. isExpanded=True is 255px, False is 65px.

On mobile this is not reflowed — it is replaced by bottom-nav. Different platform, different pattern.

In code the container is absolute, not fixed, so it respects the header above it. Collapsed items get a tooltip; expanded items must not, or the Radix portal leaks.

Naming nit: the variant values are True|false — mixed casing.

The Mes view tab strip, composed of Tab instances.

Its length is variable: Tributarias and Provisiones only exist when the user has those deduction groups enabled.

Header bar, 54px. Device = Mobile | Desktop.

Holds the live TRM chip, the notification bell, the theme toggle and the account menu. Configuración and Perfil live in that menu, not in the main navigation — which is why the nav shows four destinations for five surfaces.

Floating panel anchored to a trigger. 288px wide.

Desktop only — on mobile the same content opens in a Sheet, because a popover near the bottom of a phone screen ends up under the thumb or off-screen.

Uses surface/popover and foreground/on-popover, which are separate from the card tokens so a popover over a card still reads as a layer above it.

Mobile action menu for a list row. State = Default | Confirming.

Deleting takes two taps and the sheet stays open between them: the first tap turns the row red and rewrites it. There is no modal — the confirmation happens in place, so the user never loses sight of which entry they are deleting.

Desktop uses inline row actions instead; this component does not appear there.

The panel every form opens in. Device × Footer.

Mobile slides up from the bottom with a drag handle and rounds its top corners. Desktop slides in from the right and rounds only the left side. Different patterns, not a reflow — that is why Device is a variant and not a breakpoint.

The scrim behind it is surface/scrim, not part of this component. On mobile the sheet is clamped to the visual viewport so the keyboard never covers the fields.

Short explanation on hover or focus. Side = where it sits relative to the trigger, which is also where the arrow points.

Inverts against the page — surface/inverse with foreground/on-inverse — so it reads as an overlay and never as part of the content underneath.

Desktop only: there is no hover on touch. Anything a mobile user needs to know must be visible without one.

Legend entry for the annual donut and the 8-month trend bars.

Colour comes from data/categorical/1–5, which alias the KPI tokens — so a legend swatch can never drift from the KPI it labels.

Income row. Device = Desktop | Mobile.

These are different patterns, not a reflow: on mobile the whole row opens an edit sheet; on desktop the actions sit inline and stay visible.

Structure: icon 16px · content flex-1 min-w-0 · amount · actions. The amount uses Amount/Base.

Carries the "sin prov." marker when an income of type servicios has provisions switched off.

Expense row. Device × Schedule.

Schedule=True is a future-dated expense: it renders, but it does NOT add to the month total and does not move any account balance until its date arrives. That distinction is the whole reason this axis exists.

Recurring expenses arrive in the next month unconfirmed, so the row must also read as "needs checking".

Contribution to a savings account.

Not an expense: it does not reduce neto libre. Getting this wrong double-counted savings until the v5 migration fixed it.

Social-security line: salud, pensión, ARL.

Naming: the slash creates a phantom "ss-itemrow" group in the layer tree containing a single "ss". Rename to SSItemRow.

Transfer between the user's own accounts. Neither income nor expense — it relocates money.

Covers credit-card payments and savings contributions. Where a TRM applies, the row can show the effective rate and the implicit fee against the official one.
